instructions: Put 2 cups of rice in a pot, cover it with cold water and swirl it with your hand. Pour off the cloudy water and repeat three or four times, until the water is almost clear.

Add 2 1/4 cups fresh water to the rice and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover the pot, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered until the chicken is ready.
Meanwhile, pat the 3 lb chicken dry with paper towels and sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt over all sides.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into big chunks, about 1 1/2 inches. Cut the carrot and the onion into big chunks too.
Mince the 7 garlic cloves. Peel the ginger and cut 3 thin slices, about the size of a coin.
In a bowl, stir together 1 tbsp gochugaru, 2 tbsp gochujang, 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp mirin, 1/4 tsp black pepper and the garlic until smooth.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high. Add half the chicken, skin side down, and leave it alone for 4 to 5 minutes, until the skin is golden and lets go of the pot.
Turn the pieces and brown the other side for 2 minutes. Move them to a plate.
Add the other 1 tbsp oil and brown the rest of the chicken the same way.
Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat. Put all the chicken back in the pot with the ginger slices, the sauce and 1 1/2 cups water. Stir and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom.
Bring it to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to medium, cover the pot and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
While it simmers, cut 2 green onions into 2 inch pieces. Thinly slice the chili and put it in a small bowl for the table.
Stir the potatoes, carrot and onion into the pot, pushing them down into the sauce. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.

Take the lid off and simmer for about 5 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes and the sauce has thickened a little. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece near the bone. No thermometer? Cut into a thigh by the bone: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the green onions and 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Sprinkle 1 tsp sesame seeds over the top. Serve with the rice, with the sliced chili on the side.
method_notes: All three braise bone-in chicken pieces in a sauce of gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic, and add big chunks of potato, carrot and onion partway so they don't fall apart. Korean Bapsang's stovetop version puts the raw chicken straight into the sauce with 1 1/2 cups water, simmers it covered for 15 minutes, adds the vegetables for 10 more, then reduces it uncovered and finishes with green onions, sesame oil and seeds. Its pressure cooker version sears the chicken in batches first and adds a little doenjang. Kavey Eats (from Julian Kim's A Day in Seoul) blanches the chicken with mirim instead of searing and uses more gochujang and soy. This one sears like Korean Bapsang's pressure cooker version, then follows the stovetop method, with less gochugaru in the pot and the chili on the side.
